title: Exactly 25 controlled waves
description: Program retains exactly 25 numbered waves unless the user explicitly changes the count.

title: One wave per user turn
description: Complete exactly one wave per user turn and never silently advance to later waves.

title: Two principal ZIPs every wave
description: Every wave emits one full cumulative repository ZIP and one smaller hydration ZIP.

title: Single cumulative canonical repository
description: Each cumulative ZIP contains the entire accepted canonical repository state, never a delta-only tree.

title: Hydration state for fresh-session recovery
description: Maintain structured hydration artifacts sufficient to recover current project state with minimal drift.

title: Hydration-to-cumulative pack binding
description: Hydration pack identifies and verifies the exact cumulative ZIP via project/wave/version/hash/tree metadata.

title: Never rebuild from memory when prior repo exists
description: Future waves must inspect and mutate the prior canonical repository rather than reconstruct from model memory.

title: Preserve cumulative integrity and change history
description: Deletion, rename, replacement or material restructure must be authorized and recorded with impact/history.

title: Adaptive source-of-truth precedence
description: Use latest user instruction, invariants, governance, ADRs, docs and verified evidence in the defined precedence order.

title: Start-of-wave adaptive review
description: Every wave challenges planned scope, dependencies, blockers, over/under-engineering and future-wave impact before execution.

title: End-of-wave improvement review
description: Every wave records what was learned that should improve the remaining program.

title: Evidence-backed architecture changes
description: Material changes require identified problem, evidence/reasoning, tradeoffs, compatibility/migration/testing impact and decision record.

title: No cargo-cult technology adoption
description: Technology complexity must solve an identified requirement; popularity alone is not justification.

title: Strong defaults are revisable
description: Level-B tools/structures may be replaced by better evidence-backed alternatives without violating project invariants.

title: Open hypotheses require empirical survival
description: Level-C feature/model ideas are not requirements until validated.

title: Honest implementation status
description: Distinguish production-ready, functional starter, scaffold, interface/stub and design-only; never fabricate performance/completion.

title: Use professional defaults for minor ambiguity
description: Proceed with defensible documented defaults unless ambiguity would fundamentally change objective or safety.

title: No secrets in artifacts
description: Never include credentials, API keys, tokens or .env secrets in repository or packs.

title: Research agent cannot alter judging rules
description: Ground truth, protected periods, leakage rules, promotion criteria, BAS definition and historical results are protected from autonomous research-agent mutation.

title: Input identity is content/version based
description: Host copy suffixes do not define identity; validate internal version/structure/hash and preserve exact uploaded SHA-256.

title: Texas A&M is primary product objective
description: Optimize the product for extremely high-quality Texas A&M football forecasting.

title: Broad national historical foundation
description: Use broad FBS history to learn college-football structure; do not reduce training to A&M-only games.

title: Meaningful FCS modeling
description: Model FCS strongly enough for FBS opponents and cross-division translation.

title: Lower divisions use coarse priors with uncertainty
description: D-II/D-III/NAIA/JUCO origins receive increasingly coarse strength priors; avoid infinite recursive modeling.

title: Disproportionately deep A&M specialization
description: A&M receives higher-resolution data, state, player/unit, coaching, matchup, calibration and evaluation treatment.

title: Win and loss probabilities
description: Produce calibrated P(win) and P(loss) for Texas A&M games.

title: Team and opponent score forecasts
description: Produce coherent predicted points for A&M and opponent.

title: Expected margin forecast
description: Produce expected A&M margin consistent with score/win outputs.

title: Full outcome distributions
description: Represent uncertainty/distributions rather than only point estimates.

title: Calibrated uncertainty/confidence
description: Quantify and validate forecast uncertainty/confidence.

title: Matchup, team, unit and player strength analysis
description: Support matchup intelligence and strength estimates at team/unit/player levels where evidence allows.

title: Explainability and historical analogs
description: Provide interpretable drivers and historical analog context without implying causal certainty.

title: Pure-football and optional market-augmented forecasts
description: Maintain a market-independent forecast and a separate lane using only market data available at prediction time.

title: BAS severity outputs
description: Produce BAS probabilities for at least ≥3, ≥7, ≥14 and ≥21 point underperformance thresholds.

title: Autonomous weekly refresh/retraining/calibration
description: End-state supports automated data refresh, state updates, retraining, calibration, champion/challenger evaluation and postmortems.

title: Model/version/data lineage
description: Every prediction is traceable to model, feature set, data snapshot and source lineage.

title: Canonical internal entity IDs
source_basis: recon canonical rules; master prompt W07
description: Maintain stable internal IDs for teams, games, players, coaches, venues, institutions and other approved entities.

title: Preserve source entity mappings
description: Retain original source identifiers and confidence for source→canonical mappings.

title: Immutable raw snapshots first
description: Store external payloads/files unchanged with retrieval metadata and hashes; never overwrite historical raw state.

title: Versioned normalization contracts
description: Normalize raw fields through versioned source contracts without rewriting raw evidence.

title: Known-at/effective-dated observation semantics
description: Mutable information must carry publication/effective/retrieval semantics sufficient for as-of eligibility.

title: Absolute no-future-information leakage
description: Historical predictions may use only information available at the intended forecast timestamp.

title: Weather forecast vs observed separation
description: Do not substitute realized/observed weather for a forecast snapshot that would have existed earlier.

title: Market observations are timestamped and provider-specific
description: Never overwrite one market line; preserve provider/value/price/first-known and forecast-time cutoff semantics.

title: Future NFL Draft outcomes banned for historical roster features
description: Eventual draft outcomes cannot leak into earlier historical player/team features; only lagged completed drafts are candidates.

title: Roster/staff/depth/availability are snapshots
description: Current pages cannot retroactively reconstruct prior state without dated evidence.

title: No name-only durable production joins
description: Names may seed resolution but cannot be sole durable keys for players/coaches.

title: Units/sign conventions explicit
description: Normalize and retain original units/sign conventions for spreads, weather, elevation, distance, currency and other measures.

title: Unknown is not zero
description: Missing/uncertain values remain missing/uncertain unless an explicit validated imputation model exists.

title: Field-specific source precedence
description: Authority and precedence differ by field; A&M official sources lead A&M target facts while national structured sources lead broad data.

title: Derived features retain parent lineage
description: Every derived feature links to transform/version and parent observations where practical.

title: Full materialization profiling before production reliance
description: Measure schema, missingness, distributions, identities, timestamps, duplicates, reconciliation and drift on intended historical coverage before production reliance.

title: Recon sample statistics are not population statistics
description: Representative sample missingness/ranges/correlations cannot be presented as population findings.

title: Source access/license/redistribution governance
description: Record owner, terms, license, authentication, usage limits, redistribution and public-repo suitability.

title: PFF remains deferred/optional
source_basis: master prompt §42; recon source inventory; source log 007
description: No v1/core dependency may rely on PFF unless the user explicitly reactivates it.

title: Never bypass source controls
description: Do not bypass authentication, CAPTCHA, access controls, contractual restrictions or rate-limit protections.

title: Unclear raw redistribution defaults local-only
description: When raw redistribution rights are unclear, keep full raw data local and publish acquisition code/manifests/derived outputs only when defensible.

title: Every normalized record carries provenance/quality metadata
description: Capture source URI, retrieval/publication/effective times, versions, raw hash/path, entity mapping, units, transform and quality flags as applicable.

title: Point-in-time/leakage software tests
description: Temporal safety must be executable tests, not only documentation.

title: Canonical game is atomic split unit
description: Train/validation/test grouping occurs at canonical game identity.

title: Mirrored rows stay in same fold
description: If both team perspectives are generated, all representations of one game stay in one split.

title: Explicit game edge-case policy
description: Define neutral, postseason, overtime, FCS, canceled/rescheduled, no-contest, forfeit/vacated, relocated, duplicate-ID and classification-change behavior.

title: Raw feature registry and schema discovery
description: Inventory raw fields with source, grain, temporal class, leakage risk, family, missingness and join paths.

title: Production features require empirical evidence
description: No feature enters production solely because a human, expert or LLM believes it should matter.

title: Feature lifecycle governance
description: Track CORE/SUPPORTED/CONDITIONAL/EXPERIMENTAL/REJECTED/BANNED or evidence-backed refined equivalents without erasing history.

title: Target-specific feature selection
description: Win, score, margin and BAS may retain different feature sets based on target-specific evidence.

title: Rolling/trend/opponent-adjusted candidates
description: Evaluate rolling windows, EWMA, trends, interactions and opponent adjustment rather than assuming one hand-selected window.

title: Schedule load distinct from opponent adjustment
source_basis: recon v1.2 football mechanics; source log 011
description: Schedule stress describes what a team endured; opponent adjustment describes how impressive performance was given opposition.

title: Current team-state representation
description: Estimate underlying/available current strength from recent performance, priors, continuity, roster, staff and context rather than static season labels.

title: Old games teach football structure, not current identity
description: Old games primarily teach football structure; direct current-team influence should decay with continuity/regime change unless empirical validation supports persistence.

title: Regime/change-point awareness
description: Change-point/regime awareness is a strong modeling default to evaluate for coaching, QB, scheme and major roster changes; exact method is evidence-selected.

title: Pregame player-value system
description: Estimate player value before games using only eligible evidence and appropriate uncertainty.

title: Availability impact is player/replacement specific
description: Represent availability probability, effectiveness, expected usage, healthy value, replacement identity/value, uncertainty and matchup propagation.

title: Transfers require learned competition translation
description: Do not hard-code conference penalties; use same-player transfer cohorts, continuous competition strength, supporting cast, scheme, role and uncertainty.

title: Freshmen use separate prospect priors
description: Players with no college production use recruiting/physical/development priors rather than transfer-production translation.

title: Coach careers use effective-dated role episodes
description: Represent HC/coordinator/position/analyst roles through effective-dated episodes and responsibilities.

title: Coach effects are residual/hierarchical, not raw attribution
description: Coach effects should avoid raw attribution and favor role-conditioned residual/hierarchical controls; exact statistical representation remains evidence-selected.

title: Program resources are upstream capacity/expectation variables
description: Do not use raw dollars as automatic game bonuses; evaluate incremental value and resource-efficiency concepts after downstream football factors.

title: Public/private resource asymmetry preserved
description: Never fabricate unavailable private-school financial values; use universal baseline + public-school enrichment/explicit missingness strategy.

title: Home field is learned, not hard-coded
description: Estimate national/program/venue/era residual home effects with shrinkage; Kyle Field gets evidence-based estimate, not a fixed 12th Man bonus.

title: Expected possession/tempo subsystem
description: Model expected opportunities separately from scoring efficiency and validate its contribution.

title: Field-position/hidden-yards subsystem
description: Represent drive starts and field-position value from punts/kickoffs/turnovers/fourth downs.

title: Component-level special teams modeling
description: Evaluate kicking, punting, kickoffs, returns, blocks, continuity and weather rather than a single crude rank by default.

title: Fourth-down decision quality candidate
description: Evaluate go-for-it tendencies, conversion and EP/WP decision quality as coach/context signals.

title: Clock-management candidate
description: Evaluate timeouts, two-minute/four-minute offense, late-half sequencing and game-management residuals.

title: Score-state/garbage-time treatment
description: Score-state/garbage-time adjustment is a strong candidate treatment whose exact policy must be validated rather than assumed.

title: Effective-dated rule eras
description: Version rule changes that materially alter definitions, timing, availability, penalties or game structure.

title: Point-in-time game stakes/context candidates
description: Only objective pregame-known stakes/context definitions may be tested; retrospective labels are forbidden.

title: Officiating is experimental and anti-causal
description: Use crew history only with strong controls and pregame assignment evidence; never encode unsupported team/referee bias claims.

title: Separate pure-football and market-augmented lanes
description: Market-augmented models may use only observations known at the forecast timestamp; pure lane remains market-free.

title: Immutable prediction snapshots
description: Preserve Monday/Wednesday/Friday/pregame or refined snapshot schedule without overwriting prior forecasts.

title: Coherent joint-score/margin/win distribution
description: Score, margin, win, spread-cover and BAS residual outputs must not contradict one another.

title: Uncertainty decomposition
description: Separate epistemic/aleatoric and other uncertainty components where practical; exact decomposition is selected by validation.

title: OOD awareness widens uncertainty
description: Detect unusual states and use OOD primarily to widen uncertainty, not as an unvalidated directional correction.

title: BAS expected-margin label is strictly pregame and OOS
description: Historical expected margin for BAS must be cross-fitted or otherwise leakage-safe and cannot have seen the target game result.

title: Aggie Excess and peer comparison
description: Separate ordinary underperformance risk from A&M-specific excess and evaluate against comparable peer cohorts.

title: BAS significance/stability/anti-circularity tests
description: Test whether A&M-specific underperformance survives seasons/regimes/cohorts and is not labeling/model circularity.

title: BAS component decompositions are candidates
description: Offensive/Defensive/Special Teams/Coaching/Collapse BAS are candidate scientific decompositions, not guaranteed production models.

title: Weekly A&M Team State
description: Maintain high-resolution A&M roster/depth/QB/OL/WR/injury/transfer/recruiting/staff/scheme/workload/travel/matchup state with uncertainty.

title: A&M player/unit/coaching depth exceeds generic team
description: Allocate deeper collection/modeling effort to A&M than an arbitrary FBS team where it improves the product objective.

title: A&M-specific calibration/evaluation priority
description: Evaluate A&M separately and weight A&M performance heavily while retaining national statistical honesty.

title: A&M frequent snapshots and postmortems
description: A&M receives more frequent forecast snapshots and deep postgame error analysis without overwriting history.

title: BAS must not encode fan narrative
description: If A&M-specific excess underperformance is not statistically supported, report that result honestly.

title: BAS historical identity decays by regime/continuity
description: A&M historical identity should be shrunk by regime/continuity unless persistent effects survive controlled testing; exact decay is empirical.

title: Illustrative BAS percentages are not truth
description: Do not hard-code example percentages, hand-built fan scores or anecdotal collapse weights.

title: Strong simple baselines retained
description: Evaluate simple baselines such as Elo/logistic/score/market benchmarks and retain them for honest comparison.

title: Boosted trees are strong default candidates
description: XGBoost/LightGBM and optional CatBoost are candidate tabular champions, not sacred requirements.

title: Small PyTorch model is challenger, not assumed winner
description: A modest neural challenger may be evaluated; complexity must beat strong baselines before promotion.

title: Calibration/ensemble evaluation
description: Evaluate calibrated ensembles, proper scoring rules and model disagreement rather than arbitrary weighting.

title: Scenario/joint-score simulation is evidence-gated
description: Monte Carlo/scenario simulation may represent availability/weather/outcome uncertainty when coherent and validated.

title: Advanced sequence/graph/transformer research waits
description: Expensive/complex Phase-5 challengers are considered only after strong conventional baselines and must prove incremental value.

title: Local Windows hardware is primary target
description: Design for Ryzen 7 HX-class CPU, 32GB RAM, RTX 5060-class GPU, Windows and NVMe as the baseline environment.

title: Memory/compute-aware local processing
description: Use bounded concurrency, lazy/predicate pushdown, caching, partitioning, incremental updates and resumable pipelines.

title: Cloud GPU not mandatory for Phases 1-4
description: If remote compute is helpful, isolate it as optional; do not make core development dependent on expensive cloud GPU.

title: Autonomous dependency chain with quarantine
description: The autonomous dependency chain is a strong default ordering; implementation may refine ordering while preserving immutable raw, validation/quarantine, PIT, protected evaluation and publication correctness.

title: Champion/challenger must earn promotion
description: No automatic replacement merely because a new model exists; promotion follows protected statistical/governance gates.

title: Operational cadence differs by task
description: Daily/per-game state refresh, weekly model work and offseason research are default cadences subject to measurement.

title: Deterministic jobs use deterministic services by default
description: Do not turn deterministic ingestion/validation/state computation into LLM agents without a justified reason.

title: LLM/research agent proposes but does not self-judge
description: Agents may propose experiments/code branches but cannot alter immutable evaluation rules or directly declare promotion.

title: Protected governance is immutable/human-controlled
description: Leakage rules, protected test periods, promotion criteria, BAS headline definition and ground truth require protected control.

title: Experiment tracking/HPO tools are defaults, not mandates
description: MLflow/Optuna are current strong defaults and may be replaced through ADR if better tools satisfy requirements.

title: API/dashboard/explainability product comes after core science
description: FastAPI/Streamlit/React are candidate implementations; product surface must reflect exact snapshot/model/source metadata and warnings.

title: CI/security/observability/local operations are explicit
description: Add appropriate CI, reproducibility, security scanning, logging/metrics, backup/restore and runbooks; Docker only where useful.

title: Starter implementations carry maturity labels
description: Every code component clearly indicates production-ready/functional starter/scaffold/interface/design-only status.

title: Repository excludes large raw/model/local artifacts
description: Repository ZIPs include code/docs/schemas/tiny fixtures/manifests, not large raw datasets, huge binaries, virtualenvs, caches or local experiment stores.

title: Stable requirement IDs are never cosmetically renumbered
description: Accepted requirement IDs persist through revisions/supersession for traceability.

title: Stable ADR history preserved
description: Architectural decisions receive stable IDs and preserve changes/supersessions.

title: Wave 06 performs fresh comprehensive data-universe research
description: Search beyond reconnaissance/familiar sources across football data domains, PIT/access/license/fallback/value questions and update later waves when justified.

title: Wave 24 refreshes source landscape and challenges architecture
description: Run targeted source refresh and ask whether major architecture decisions should be kept/revised/deferred/rejected using implementation evidence.

title: Wave 25 performs final consolidation and Codex handoff
description: Audit repository/requirements/ADRs/data/PIT/features/architecture/acceptance and produce final implementation order and handoff.

title: Wave 01 reads all source logs in numeric order
description: Read every supplied TXT source log; numeric sequence 001→020 is authoritative rather than ZIP archive entry order.

title: Wave 01 reads mandatory recon chain and extension policies/schemas
description: Read prescribed reconnaissance files and all policy/schema files under v1.1 and v1.2 before finalizing source synthesis.

title: Minimal src-layout package scaffold
description: W02 used a minimal installable src scaffold and deliberately deferred domain/service decomposition; W03 subsequently refined the architecture through ADR-052.

title: Preferred local Python 3.12 baseline
description: Prefer CPython 3.12 locally; permit nearby supported minors during starter planning until model-library compatibility is benchmarked.

title: Portable venv plus pip bootstrap baseline
description: Standard Python venv/pip must be sufficient to bootstrap; optional faster environment managers cannot become mandatory without evidence.

title: Executable repository integrity command
description: Provide one cross-platform command that checks required structure, manifest coverage/hashes, governance IDs, secrets and forbidden artifacts.

title: Deterministic non-self-referential manifests
description: Generate tree/manifest/hash evidence deterministically while excluding manifest/hash files from their own scope.

title: ZIP path safety before extraction
description: Reject absolute, drive-qualified and parent-traversal ZIP members before extraction of wave artifacts.

title: Hydration allowlist is machine-readable
description: Generate hydration packs from an explicit source-to-archive allowlist plus generated binding/recovery/hash files.

title: Local and CI validation use same commands
description: Minimal CI must call the same repository-integrity and unit-test commands used locally to reduce environment divergence.

title: Cross-platform repository operations
description: Repository tooling uses pathlib/Python and is exercised on Windows and Linux CI; Windows wrappers remain thin operators.

title: Codex worktree isolation contract
description: Use focused worktrees/branches and prohibit uncoordinated parallel mutation of unfrozen shared contracts/protected governance.

title: Codex branch naming default
description: Default isolated branch convention is codex/<epic>-<task>, revisable if repository workflow later requires another convention.

title: Do not freeze Wave03 domain boundaries in W02
description: Wave02 establishes operational structure only and deliberately defers detailed service/domain/module architecture to Wave03.

title: Windows PowerShell operator wrappers
description: Provide thin PowerShell wrappers for bootstrap, validation, prior-wave verification, packaging and worktree creation.

title: Repository line-ending and path portability policy
description: Normalize text line endings through .gitattributes/.editorconfig and use project-relative/pathlib paths in Python.

title: Deterministic cumulative ZIP content order
description: Cumulative/hydration ZIP members are sorted and normalized so identical staged bytes yield identical archives.

title: Completed wave pair validator
description: Validate cumulative SHA binding, hydration required files/hashes, safe ZIP paths and cumulative internal manifest before handoff.

title: Wave02 CI remains minimal scaffold
description: W02 CI covers repository/tool integrity only; full security/dependency/deployment/observability CI is deferred to W23 unless required earlier.

title: No unverified tool-specific Codex config schema
description: Do not commit guessed external-tool configuration formats; keep Codex operating contracts as documented repository files until a schema is verified and useful.

title: Offline-first modular monolith default
description: Use one local modular application/repository by default; split deployable services only when independent scaling/security/latency evidence justifies it.

title: Pregame product uses immutable snapshot serving
source_basis: W03 architecture comparison; prediction snapshot principle
description: Dashboard/API should read immutable forecast snapshots rather than synchronously run ingestion/features/models per request.

title: Production forecast path does not require research agents
description: Core forecast refresh must not import or require research-agent execution.

title: LLM is optional assistive capability
description: The deterministic core forecast runtime must not require an LLM. LLM-assisted extraction/research/explanation remains optional and evidence-governed.

title: Layered immutable data zones
source_basis: Recon canonical data rules; master storage principles
description: Represent raw, quarantine, canonical, PIT state, features, training, model artifacts and forecast snapshots as versioned/immutable zones.

title: PIT state is mandatory feature gateway
description: Feature construction must consume eligible as-of state rather than arbitrary current/provider state.

title: Training and inference share feature contracts
description: Training/evaluation and forecast inference must use the same feature-definition and PIT semantics.

title: Provider details isolated behind source adapters
description: Provider-specific retrieval/parsing must not leak into football model logic.

title: Canonical identity separate from source identity remains architectural boundary
description: Stable canonical IDs and source mappings remain distinct from raw/source IDs.

title: National-to-A&M specialization interface is explicit
description: A&M specialization must communicate with the national foundation through an explicit interface while leaving residual/multi-task/MoE statistical form open to later evidence.

title: A&M specialization cannot fork canonical truth
description: A&M official evidence may receive field-specific precedence but maps into the same canonical/PIT system.

title: A&M specialization may collapse to no adjustment
description: Architecture must permit shrinkage/null A&M-specific effect rather than force an Aggie-specific correction.

title: Forecast outputs are coherently assembled
description: Win, score, margin and BAS-related outputs must be composed through a coherent forecast-distribution boundary.

title: BAS consumes leakage-safe expected performance
description: BAS runtime/labels depend on PIT-safe expected margin/forecast information, never same-game hindsight.

title: Pure-football and market-augmented lanes remain separable
description: A market-augmented forecast cannot overwrite or obscure the corresponding market-free forecast.

title: Future live lane isolated from pregame
description: Live/in-game information must not feed the pregame feature row for the same game.

title: Parquet plus DuckDB preferred early analytical implementation
source_basis: Local hardware; master storage defaults; W03 comparison
description: Use partitioned Parquet and DuckDB as preferred early local analytical stack, subject to later evidence.

title: PostgreSQL is optional behind a storage boundary
description: Do not require PostgreSQL until canonical review/concurrency/transactional workloads justify it; preserve an adapter boundary.

title: No online feature store required for pregame v1
description: Do not add a network online feature store solely for pregame snapshot serving.

title: No Kafka Redis Kubernetes or microservices requirement in current architecture
description: These technologies remain available only if later operational evidence creates a real requirement.

title: Serving cannot bypass snapshot publication
description: Read-serving surfaces must consume published forecast snapshots rather than raw/PIT/model internals directly.

title: Research outputs enter production only through protected evaluation
description: Experiment artifacts/proposals cannot self-promote; protected evaluation/promotion remains the gate.

title: Architecture registry is machine-readable
description: Maintain a machine-readable architecture registry while it remains the best anti-drift mechanism; an evidence-backed ADR may replace the representation without weakening architecture conformance.

title: Architecture dependency rules are executable tests
description: Validate component IDs/import graph, plane isolation, PIT gateway and live/LLM restrictions in repository validation.

title: Batch stages are resumable and quarantine failures
description: Design batch/forecast-refresh stages to checkpoint immutable artifacts and quarantine bad data rather than silently coerce it.

title: W03 freezes semantic interfaces not later-wave schemas or statistical families
description: Do not preempt W07/W08/W14/W16/W21/W22 ownership by freezing detailed entity schemas, PIT internals, model families, orchestrator or frontend technology.

title: Acceptance evidence is explicit and traceable
description: Every active/default/research requirement maps to one or more acceptance controls, evidence modes and owning waves; no material requirement remains acceptance-unmapped.

title: Requirement lifecycle is separate from acceptance evidence state
description: Constraint class and lifecycle status do not imply that implementation evidence already exists; acceptance evidence state is tracked independently.

title: Protected acceptance controls cannot be relaxed by research agents
description: Leakage, ground-truth, protected-test and promotion controls remain protected from autonomous experimenter mutation.

title: Do not fabricate quantitative acceptance thresholds
description: Unknown model/data/performance thresholds are recorded as evidence-pending and assigned to an owning wave rather than filled with arbitrary numbers.

title: Every active Level-A requirement has a blocking or mandatory acceptance contract
description: Each active Level-A requirement maps to at least one mandatory acceptance control at the gate where the requirement becomes applicable.

title: Level-B defaults have explicit revisit/change semantics
description: Strong defaults remain accepted current choices but their acceptance mapping records the evidence/review needed to keep or replace them.

title: Level-C hypotheses remain nonblocking until promoted
description: A Level-C hypothesis cannot block core release or be treated as production truth before an approved experiment promotes it.

title: External inputs cross an explicit trust boundary
description: Files, archives, APIs, scraped documents and LLM-derived extractions are untrusted inputs until path/schema/type/provenance checks appropriate to the source succeed.

title: Source records are schema/contract validated before canonical acceptance
description: Malformed or contract-violating source records cannot silently enter canonical or training state.

title: Data/source content cannot trigger arbitrary code execution
description: Treat source content as data; never execute embedded instructions, macros, scripts or serialized code merely because a source provides them.

title: Secrets remain externalized with least-privilege access
description: Credentials are provided through approved local/CI secret mechanisms, scoped to minimum required access and never persisted in forecast/data artifacts.

title: Dependencies and executable tooling retain provenance/integrity evidence
description: Record dependency/tool versions and use integrity/security checks appropriate to the finalized dependency surface.

title: Logs and diagnostics cannot expose secrets or restricted raw data
description: Operational logs use structured identifiers/metrics and redact credentials and restricted raw payloads; debugging convenience cannot override source restrictions.

title: Forecast snapshots are replayable from lineage
description: A published forecast links sufficient model/config/feature/data snapshot lineage to reproduce or explain the exact historical forecast without querying mutable current state.

title: Deterministic transforms are versioned and testable
description: Canonicalization, PIT selection, labels and deterministic feature transforms have versioned definitions and fixture/replay tests.

title: Training and forecast environments are captured
description: Record Python/package/model-runtime/config versions needed to reproduce training/evaluation and forecast execution.

title: Stochastic processes record seeds/configuration
description: Where stochastic algorithms are used, persist relevant seeds, sampling configuration and library/runtime versions; nondeterminism must be explicit.

title: Training/evaluation/model artifacts are immutable and linked
description: Training matrix, evaluation result, calibration result and model artifact identities are immutable/versioned and linked through lineage.

title: Invalid data is quarantined rather than silently coerced
description: Records that fail material data-contract or temporal checks enter a visible quarantine/review path and cannot silently become valid through permissive coercion.

title: Entity-resolution uncertainty remains visible
description: Ambiguous mappings retain candidate evidence/confidence/review state and cannot be silently auto-accepted without an evidence-backed policy.

title: Data-quality gates are domain/grain specific
description: Completeness, uniqueness, range and reconciliation checks are defined per source/domain/grain; one arbitrary global quality threshold is prohibited.

title: Source missingness/outage behavior is explicit
description: Each production-critical source/domain defines whether absence causes quarantine, degraded-mode uncertainty, fallback use or forecast suppression.

title: PIT ambiguity fails closed
description: When known-at eligibility cannot be proven for a mutable field, classify it unsafe/review-required and exclude it from protected historical features until resolved.

title: Performance budgets are measured on target hardware before freezing thresholds
description: Benchmark representative/full workloads on the target local environment before setting hard runtime/RAM/storage acceptance limits.

title: Peak RAM, runtime and disk footprint are measured for material workloads
description: Track peak memory, elapsed time and storage footprint for ingestion, PIT/features, training/evaluation and forecast refresh on representative/full data.

title: Performance optimization cannot weaken correctness
description: Caching, parallelism, approximations or incremental processing may not bypass PIT, provenance, validation, split or acceptance rules.

title: Forecast freshness is explicit to users and operators
description: Every served forecast exposes snapshot/as-of time and freshness state; stale results are never mislabeled as current.

title: Acceptance architecture supports multiple evidence modes
description: Acceptance may require static checks, unit/integration tests, chronological replay, scientific evaluation, benchmark evidence or manual/legal review as appropriate.

title: Critical temporal/leakage controls are release-blocking
description: A failing protected PIT/leakage/split-safety control blocks the affected dataset/model/forecast from promotion or publication.

title: Promotion criteria are fixed before protected-test inspection
description: Model/feature promotion rules and protected evaluation windows are versioned before protected results are inspected for a promotion decision.

title: Protected test results are not iterative tuning feedback
description: Repeated tuning against a protected test period is prohibited; exhausted test periods are documented and replaced prospectively rather than relabeled.

title: Acceptance failures produce traceable remediation
description: Blocking failures identify affected controls/requirements/evidence and create a repair/retest path rather than being waived silently.

title: Architecture changes update acceptance contracts
description: A material ADR that changes system boundaries also updates affected acceptance controls and traceability in the same controlled change.

title: W04 acceptance contracts do not imply later implementation completion
description: Mark future-wave controls as defined/pending rather than PASS when their implementation/data/model evidence does not yet exist.

title: Future redistribution/publication review
description: Private local acquisition and training are authorized. Before raw third-party artifacts are publicly redistributed or commercialized, perform a separate review for that proposed act; never publish raw data by default.

title: User-facing forecasts expose lineage and uncertainty metadata
description: Forecast surfaces expose snapshot time, model/version lineage, market-lane identity, uncertainty/confidence state and material warning/freshness flags.

title: Labels are versioned with temporal semantics
description: Outcome/BAS/derived labels have versioned definitions, source provenance and cutoff semantics; label revisions do not silently rewrite prior experiments.

title: Monitoring appends observations rather than rewriting history
description: Monitoring, error analysis and postmortems append new evidence/status while immutable historical forecasts/models/data remain unchanged.

title: Manual acceptance decisions require named rationale/evidence
description: Where automation cannot decide licensing, ambiguous semantics or architecture exceptions, the manual decision records reviewer role, rationale, evidence and date/version.

title: Five-phase implementation WBS
description: Maintain an explicit five-phase implementation plan with epics/tasks/dependencies rather than a prose-only roadmap.

title: Stable epic and task IDs
description: Epic/task IDs remain stable after acceptance; superseded work is preserved rather than renumbered.

title: Requirement-to-task exact coverage
description: Every cumulative requirement maps to at least one implementation/governance/research task appropriate to its lifecycle.

title: Acceptance-control-to-task coverage
description: Every acceptance control maps to one or more tasks that create or maintain its evidence.

title: Implementation dependency graph is acyclic
description: Task dependencies form a valid DAG; blocked work may not bypass prerequisite gates.

title: Dependency-critical spine is explicit
description: Identify the dependency-critical program spine without pretending it is a duration-based schedule critical path.

title: No fabricated schedule precision
description: Do not invent hours/dates/velocity estimates without measured evidence or explicit user scheduling input.

title: Complexity classes describe coordination not hours
description: Use bounded complexity classes based on coupling/uncertainty/protected-contract risk rather than time estimates.

title: Mandatory W06 backlog replan gate
description: After fresh data research, explicitly reassess and revise source-dependent W07-W25 backlog before those tasks become ready.

title: Source-dependent future tasks remain provisional before W06
description: Tasks whose source/schema assumptions may change in W06 are labeled for revalidation rather than treated as frozen.

title: Codex work packet schema
description: Codex work is issued as bounded packets with scope, dependencies, artifacts, tests, acceptance IDs and stop conditions.

title: Shared-contract mutation serialization
description: Unfrozen shared contracts are mutated by one owning workstream at a time; dependent parallel work waits or targets stable interfaces.

title: Worktree isolation for parallel mutations
description: Parallel Codex implementation uses isolated worktrees/branches and explicit integration order.

title: Evidence gate before merge/adoption
description: A task is not DONE merely because code exists; required tests/evidence/acceptance controls must pass before integration.

title: Autonomous queue respects protected controls
description: Automated work selection cannot rewrite protected evaluation/leakage/promotion criteria to make its own work pass.

title: Task maturity/status honesty
description: Task states distinguish planned, blocked, ready, in-progress, evidence-pending, done, rejected and superseded work.

title: Task outputs are explicit
description: Every material task declares expected artifacts/evidence rather than an ambiguous activity-only description.

title: Task wave ownership is explicit
description: Every task declares its primary owner wave even when its capability phase spans multiple waves.

title: Capability phases do not override 25-wave execution
description: Five implementation phases organize capability dependencies but never create extra waves or silently reorder user-governed wave execution.

title: Dependency edges are machine-readable
description: Task dependency edges are stored in a machine-readable artifact and validated.

title: Critical path semantics are dependency-based
description: Critical-path labeling means downstream dependency centrality/gating, not estimated elapsed time.

title: W05 must not execute later-wave implementation
description: Wave05 plans implementation but does not perform W06 research or W07+ football implementation.

title: Backlog plan is versioned and provenance-linked
description: Backlog/phase/epic/task artifacts record plan version and are updated through adaptive change history.

title: Codex mutation scope is explicit
description: Work packets specify allowed mutation scope and shared-contract exclusions to reduce conflicting autonomous changes.

title: Priority is adaptive after evidence gates
description: Within invariant dependencies, implementation priority may be revised when research, evidence or constraints show a higher-value ordering.

title: Wave06 uses fresh current source research
description: W06 must research the current source universe beyond the reconnaissance pack using current primary/official/provider evidence.

title: Wave06 searches beyond CFBD and SportsDataverse
description: W06 cannot stop at already-known public sources and must investigate governing bodies, conferences, schools, academic/public and optional commercial alternatives.

title: Source research queries and evidence are logged
description: Research date, discovery queries, source reviewed, conclusions and follow-ups are preserved.

title: Important data domains retain primary and fallback source decisions
description: Each material domain records primary/fallback/remaining gap rather than assuming one provider is permanent.

title: Historical weather forecasts preserve issued model-run provenance
description: Historical weather features use forecasts actually issued by cutoff with provider/model/run initialization/lead/valid-time provenance.

title: Observed weather remains separate from forecast weather
description: Observed/reanalysis weather may verify/label conditions but cannot replace an earlier issued forecast in a historical forecast row.

title: Official conference availability reports are primary when covered
description: When an official availability policy covers a game/report time, versioned official reports outrank aggregator/media inference.

title: Availability coverage scope and noncoverage are explicit
description: Conference, season, conference-game/nonconference and report-time scope is recorded; missing outside coverage is UNKNOWN, not healthy/available.

title: Lower-division official statistics support bounded strength priors
description: Use NCAA/NAIA/NJCAA official statistics where practical for opponent/transfer translation without recursively matching FBS resolution.

title: Regulatory environment is effective-dated
description: Playing, roster, eligibility, transfer and other materially relevant regulatory changes are represented by adoption/publication/effective semantics.

title: Market enrichment requires timestamped observations
description: Market-augmented forecasts use provider/book/market observations demonstrably known by cutoff; paid data may be optional but closing/future lines cannot leak.

title: Derived sources retain upstream provenance
description: Derived repositories/APIs record upstream publisher/source lineage so overlaps are not mistaken for independent evidence.

title: Commercial sources remain optional until value is proven
description: Licensed feeds do not become core Phase1-4 dependencies without evidence-backed ADR covering value/cost/rights/fallback.

title: Source access/license/redistribution classification is maintained
description: Every production source records owner/access/auth/cost/terms/redistribution/attribution/public-repo suitability and is re-reviewed when changed.

title: Private-resource proxies are not mislabeled football spending
description: IRS/institutional proxy values remain semantically distinct from football-specific spending and carry uncertainty/missingness.

title: Poll/ranking observations are publication-dated
description: AP/AFCA/CFP or other rankings enter historical features only after the relevant ranking release was public.

title: Source status is refreshed after W06
description: W24 compares APIs, report policies, archives, terms, availability and source quality against this W06 baseline.

title: W06 replan gate must clear before W07 source-dependent work
description: W06 explicitly revises/clears future source-dependent backlog after research; W07 may not start before this gate passes.

title: A&M uses SEC availability reports as highest-confidence recent official lane
description: For covered SEC conference games from the official-report era, A&M availability reconstruction prioritizes official SEC report versions.

title: Acquired source evidence is immutable and hash/provenance linked
description: Raw source payloads/documents keep retrieval metadata, source URL/ID, hashes and applicable publication/effective timestamps before canonical transformation.

title: Canonical IDs are opaque and nonsemantic
description: Canonical surrogate IDs must not encode source IDs, team/name/season, or mutable business meaning.

title: Assigned canonical IDs are never renumbered or reused
description: Once materialized/assigned, a canonical ID remains stable; corrections use supersession/redirect/split history rather than ID reuse.

title: Canonical entity type namespace is explicit
description: Every canonical ID belongs to an explicit entity type; cross-type key collisions cannot silently resolve.

title: Football season identity is distinct from fiscal/academic year
description: Football season uses the football season year; fiscal/academic/resource years remain separate fields/observations.

title: Source entity keys are source- and type-scoped
description: Durable source mappings are scoped by source system, entity type and source entity key, with context retained.

title: Name-only durable entity joins are prohibited
description: Names may generate candidates but cannot by themselves establish durable player/coach/source-to-canonical production identity.

title: Aliases are scoped and history-preserving
description: Aliases retain source/context and temporal scope rather than overwriting historical names.

title: Player identity persists across transfers and role changes
source_basis: Recon A&M roster identity policy; W07
description: Transfers/team/position/class changes create membership/observation episodes, not new player identities.

title: Coach identity is independent of team and role
description: Coach role/team/title/play-caller changes are effective-dated role episodes linked to stable coach identity.

title: Team and institution identities remain distinct
description: Football team/program identity and institution identity use an explicit affiliation/crosswalk instead of string equivalence.

title: Game identity is separate from schedule mutations
source_basis: Recon join contracts; master edge cases; W07
description: Kickoff/venue/status/home-away-neutral changes are observations; same-contest reschedules may retain identity, replacement matchups create new identity.

title: Venue identity is separate from mutable venue attributes
description: Venue names, coordinates corrections, capacity, surface and roof state are observations/episodes, not identity.

title: Conference membership is an effective-dated relationship
description: Conference membership/classification changes do not create a new team identity and must be represented as episodes.

title: Official identity uncertainty remains explicit
description: Name-only or weak officiating evidence remains unresolved/reviewable; uncertain officials are not silently conflated.

title: Source evidence identity is layered
description: Separate source system, resource family, publication version, raw capture and source observation identities.

title: Retrieval-event identity is preserved even for identical bytes
description: Identical raw hashes at different retrieval times may share content but do not erase distinct retrieval/capture evidence.

title: Entity resolution decisions are append-only and auditable
description: Mapping/review decisions retain method, evidence and supersession history rather than being destructively edited.

title: Fuzzy matching cannot auto-accept without labeled evidence
description: Fuzzy/name-context matching may rank candidates but cannot auto-promote to canonical truth until a labeled benchmark supports a protected threshold/policy.

title: Entity merge/split corrections preserve historical lineage
description: Duplicate merges use redirects and splits append corrected mappings/new identities while preserving prior versions/decisions.

title: Unresolved resolution is a valid explicit state
description: Ambiguous records remain unresolved/review-required and cannot be forced to a top candidate merely to keep a pipeline moving.

title: Relational persistence remains conditional behind storage ports
description: Do not require PostgreSQL for current single-writer append-only identity workflows; preserve storage boundaries and reopen on demonstrated transactional/concurrency need.

title: Entity auto-accept thresholds require labeled resolver evaluation
description: THR-008 or equivalent automatic ambiguous-resolution threshold may only be set from labeled resolution/review evidence, not intuition.

title: Knowledge and validity time are separate axes
description: Public knowability and real-world applicability must be represented and evaluated separately.

title: PIT timestamps are timezone-aware and normalized
description: Normalized temporal fields use timezone-aware timestamps (UTC convention) while raw source values remain preserved in provenance.

title: Raw source temporal values are preserved
description: Normalization may not erase original source timestamp/value text or source version lineage.

title: first_known_at requires defensible evidence
description: Earliest public knowability must be evidence-backed; season labels/current pages cannot establish it.

title: Unknown temporal eligibility fails closed
description: Ambiguous/missing temporal evidence is review/quarantine/ineligible rather than guessed into a feature row.

title: Publication revisions preserve historical replay
description: Later corrections/reports cannot rewrite earlier snapshots; as-of replay selects the version knowable then.

title: As-of joins require knowledge and target validity
description: As-of selection requires knowledge cutoff plus target validity/effective applicability where relevant.

title: Future-effective known facts may support future targets
description: A fact known before its effective date may be eligible for a forecast of a target event inside its future valid interval.

title: Retrospective evidence requires dated corroboration
description: Current/retrospective bios/pages are historical-ineligible unless dated evidence proves the fact/version was knowable at cutoff.

title: Historical game outputs require completion before feature cutoff
description: Same/future game outputs are banned; prior-game outputs can enter later-game features only after completion and source knowability.

title: Forecast and replay cutoffs are immutable versioned records
description: Every feature reconstruction/forecast/replay references an immutable cutoff and temporal-policy version.

title: Cutoffs preserve target and lane provenance
description: Cutoff lineage records target game/event time, prediction timestamp, forecast lane, data snapshot and purpose.

title: As-of selection is deterministic and lineage-returning
description: Equal inputs/policy produce the same selected observation IDs and lineage; selectors do not return bare mutable values.

title: Market observations remain provider and timestamp scoped
description: Market lane uses immutable provider/market/side observations known by cutoff.

title: Market snapshot labels do not override timestamp eligibility
description: Opening/current/closing classification is descriptive and cannot substitute for actual knowability at the forecast cutoff.

title: Weather forecasts preserve exact model-run timing
description: Issued weather evidence preserves model initialization, availability/first-known, forecast-valid time, lead and retrieval lineage.

title: Observed weather cannot replace earlier issued forecast
description: Historical pregame snapshots use weather forecasts available then, not realized/observed conditions learned later.

title: Availability reports preserve policy and version scope
description: Availability observations retain report policy, applicable game scope, report sequence/version and temporal provenance.

title: Availability noncoverage is unknown not healthy
description: Missing report/non-covered game may not be inferred as player availability.

title: Availability revisions do not rewrite earlier snapshots
description: A later availability report version affects only cutoffs at/after its defensible first-known time.

title: Roster/staff/depth state is effective-dated and knowledge-safe
description: Mutable roster/staff/depth observations require both applicability and as-of public-knowledge semantics.

title: Regulatory publication and effective intervals are separate
description: Rule/eligibility/roster/transfer regulations preserve publication/first-known separately from effective intervals.

title: Resource reporting period does not establish knowability
description: Financial/resource period labels are separate from public publication/first-known timestamps.

title: Future draft/postseason/final-season outcomes are banned
description: Eventual outcomes unavailable at the historical cutoff cannot be used as direct historical pregame features.

title: PIT gateway is mandatory feature-entry boundary
description: Feature construction consumes PIT-safe state through CMP-005 and cannot directly query mutable raw/current source state.

title: Protected synthetic leakage battery is mandatory
description: PIT contract changes must preserve/extend synthetic leakage scenarios and protected tests.

title: prediction_eligible_at is derived under policy version
description: prediction_eligible_at is derived/cache metadata, not an authoritative raw source timestamp or sole eligibility predicate.

title: Retrieval time is conservative fallback for unknown earlier availability
description: When earlier public availability cannot be defensibly reconstructed, retrieval time or documented conservative lag is used instead of guessing.

title: Prediction snapshots retain domain cutoff lineage
description: Forecast snapshots link exact data snapshot and market/weather/availability cutoffs or equivalent observation lineage.

title: Historical training replay has a model-training cutoff
description: A historical training run may train only on game labels completed/known before its training cutoff while each example uses its own pregame feature cutoff.

title: Raw fields require stable source-scoped registry identity
description: Every documented/materialized raw field has a stable raw_field_id scoped to source/dataset/field semantics.

title: Raw field registry preserves provenance
description: Registry records source ID, dataset/model, exact field path and classification origin.

title: Verified reconnaissance temporal classes are preserved
description: Schema scanning cannot silently downgrade or overwrite verified prior temporal/leakage classifications.

title: Unknown source schemas are explicit
description: W06 endpoints without enumerated schemas remain SCHEMA_PENDING_MATERIALIZATION; fields are not invented.

title: Documented and observed types are separate
description: Scanner-observed types do not overwrite documented source types or historical schema versions.

title: Schema discovery is deterministic and bounded
description: For the same input and scan limit, scanner output is deterministic and records records-scanned.

title: Schema drift is recorded rather than silently mutated
description: Field additions/removals/type changes create drift evidence and do not rewrite historical registry state.

title: Schema scanner does not execute source code
description: Discovery parses supported data formats only and never executes scripts/instructions embedded in source data.

title: Nested JSON uses explicit field paths
description: Nested object fields use deterministic dotted paths or an approved versioned equivalent.

title: Parquet scanner support is optional until dependency justified
description: Parquet scanning may use pyarrow when present but does not make it a mandatory W09 dependency.

title: Sample missingness is not population missingness
description: Recon sample profiles remain representative evidence only; population missingness is measured on materialized snapshots.

title: Population missingness defaults to unmeasured
description: Raw fields remain UNMEASURED_UNTIL_SOURCE_MATERIALIZATION unless source-specific population evidence exists.

title: Join-key presence does not prove semantic compatibility
description: Join fields require canonical identity/mapping and semantic validation; name/key presence alone is insufficient.

title: Name-only durable cross-source joins remain forbidden
description: Raw-field join metadata preserves W07 canonical identity policy.

title: Exact field-name overlap is not semantic duplication
description: Same-name fields require grain/unit/definition/temporal/join review before consolidation.

title: Source-level redundancy decisions are preserved
description: W09 imports W06 source-overlap decisions rather than replacing them with field-name heuristics.

title: Raw-field registration never implies predictive usefulness
description: Registry presence/status is metadata only and cannot promote a production feature.

title: Banned fields cannot enter W10 candidate experiments
description: POSTGAME_OR_FUTURE_BANNED fields have no W10 candidate handoff.

title: Review-required fields fail closed at W10 handoff
description: REVIEW_REQUIRED fields cannot enter candidate experiments until temporal classification is resolved.

title: Historical outputs require PIT-safe prior-game derivation
description: HISTORICAL_AGGREGATE_ONLY fields may hand off only as prior-game/PIT-safe aggregation inputs.

title: As-of fields require W08 reconstruction
description: ASOF_RECONSTRUCTION_REQUIRED fields remain behind the protected PIT gateway.

title: Effective snapshot fields require W08 snapshot selection
description: SAFE_ONLY_WITH_EFFECTIVE_SNAPSHOT fields require target-valid as-of state.

title: Direct pregame candidates still require PIT and data-quality gates
description: DIRECT_PREGAME_CANDIDATE is not unconditional safety or production adoption.

title: Feature-family labels are organizational not promotion evidence
description: Inherited feature-family tags help organize experiments but do not establish usefulness.

title: Raw-field records carry source license/access context
description: Registry preserves source access priority/license/redistribution status for acquisition/publication decisions.

title: W09 handoff states are explicit and machine-readable
description: Every raw field has a governed handoff state controlling whether W10 candidate design is permitted.

title: Raw-field IDs are not silently repurposed after schema rename
description: Semantic rename/repurpose creates a new raw-field identity and controlled supersession.

title: Feature registry contract is executable
description: Repository validation checks registry counts, identities, temporal preservation, missingness honesty and handoff safety.

title: Feature transforms consume PIT state only
description: Every predictive transform consumes W08-eligible PIT state; no direct mutable-provider/current-state access.

title: Trailing transforms exclude target game
description: Rolling/lag/EWMA/trend transforms for pregame prediction use observations strictly before the target cutoff/game.

title: Feature transforms are versioned and parameterized
description: Derived candidates preserve transform ID/version/parameters and parent/cutoff lineage.

title: No universal rolling window is assumed
description: Candidate windows/recency parameters are compared chronologically rather than hard-coding one universal window from intuition.

title: Population data quality precedes promotion
description: Feature promotion requires materialized population coverage/missingness/schema evidence; representative samples are insufficient.

title: Redundancy decisions require conditional evidence
description: Same-name/correlated predictors are not automatically merged or deleted; assess semantic and conditional value.

title: Univariate association is exploratory only
description: Correlation or mutual information alone cannot promote a production feature.

title: Model importance alone cannot promote features
description: Regularization/tree/permutation/importance methods provide evidence but no single importance method is a sufficient promotion gate.

title: Permutation evidence is out-of-fold and chronological
description: Permutation importance used for decisions is evaluated on chronological validation evidence rather than training fit.

title: Feature-family ablation required before promotion
description: Promoted feature families require chronological full-vs-without-family evidence under the target evaluation plan.

title: Temporal stability required before promotion
description: Feature/family value is assessed across declared chronological folds/seasons/eras before production promotion.

title: Critical subgroup and A&M stability are assessed
description: Where relevant, feature evidence includes A&M and predeclared critical subgroup performance, without cherry-picked promotion.

title: Lifecycle state is target specific
description: A feature/family can hold different lifecycle states for win, margin, score and BAS targets.

title: Market feature lifecycle is isolated from pure-football lane
description: Market-derived candidates cannot enter the pure-football feature set; they are evaluated only in market-augmented experiments.

title: Feature lifecycle history is append only
description: Promotion/demotion/rejection history is preserved with evidence references; old decisions are not silently erased.

title: Rejected features reopen only with material new basis
description: A rejected feature/family returns to EXPERIMENTAL only under a new experiment/data/transform hypothesis while prior rejection remains recorded.

title: BANNED means structural prohibition
description: BANNED features cannot become usable due to predictive performance; underlying safety/rights classification must first be corrected.

title: Feature promotion criteria are precommitted
description: Promotion/evaluation rules are versioned before protected feature evaluation to limit selection-on-test leakage.

title: Derived feature lineage is replayable
description: Candidate/production features retain raw parents, transform/version/parameters, PIT cutoff and experiment lineage sufficient for replay.

title: Synthetic W10 tests cannot establish predictive value
description: Synthetic transform/screening tests prove code semantics only; they cannot create empirical lifecycle promotions.

title: Backward elimination is optional
description: Backward elimination may be evaluated where useful but is not a universal required feature-selection algorithm.

title: Feature complexity must earn value
description: When predictive evidence is similar, prefer lower compute/storage/maintenance complexity; measured cost evidence is used when available.

title: Team-state snapshots are immutable at forecast cutoff
description: Every team-state artifact is bound to an immutable forecast cutoff/version and cannot be overwritten in place.

title: Separate prior, underlying, available strength and recent form
description: Do not collapse prior strength, underlying quality, forecast-time available strength and recent-form evidence into one static rating.

title: Underlying strength is dynamic state, not a static season label
description: Underlying strength may evolve with PIT-safe evidence and uncertainty; it is not a permanent preseason or ranking label.

title: Available-strength detailed player adjustments remain W12-owned
description: W11 freezes the available-strength interface but does not fabricate player-specific availability/replacement adjustments before W12 evidence.

title: Week-1 prior is composite rather than single-source
description: Evaluate composite priors using prior performance and PIT-safe roster/recruiting/transfer/coaching/resource/development evidence as available.

title: Every prior input obeys PIT and provenance
description: No prior component may use information unavailable at the historical forecast cutoff.

title: Prior component weights require empirical evidence
description: Do not manually freeze prior-component weights from intuition.

title: Prior-to-current-season blend schedule is empirical
description: Week/game-specific prior decay or observed-evidence gain remains an experiment parameter selected chronologically.

title: Program resources are upstream early-season candidates
description: Resource variables are candidate preseason/program-capacity inputs, not direct weekly point bonuses.

title: Separate national-history utility from current-team relevance
description: An old game may remain useful nationally while carrying low relevance for the present team/regime.

title: Recency weighting is a research candidate, not a fixed rule
description: Evaluate recency weighting against baselines; illustrative historical decay examples are not requirements.

title: Regime similarity uses effective-dated continuity evidence
description: Candidate regime relevance may use coach/coordinator/QB/roster/scheme continuity only from PIT-safe effective-dated evidence.

title: Change points do not automatically erase pre-change history
description: A regime-break candidate may trigger shrinkage or uncertainty expansion; hard resets require empirical justification.

title: Distinguish football regime changes from data-coverage changes
description: Schema/source coverage shifts cannot be interpreted as football performance change without evidence.

title: Continuity factors remain separately auditable
description: Keep major continuity factors individually traceable so a composite similarity score can be ablated and audited.

title: Every opponent has strength estimate and uncertainty
description: Opponent representation includes continuous strength and uncertainty regardless of division.

title: FCS receives strong secondary modeling
description: Use FCS internal competition plus FCS-FBS evidence rather than treating FCS as a single fixed class penalty.

title: D-II support is bounded/coarse
description: Use basic D-II ratings/results where useful without making full D-II analytics a project prerequisite.

title: D-III/NAIA/JUCO support is increasingly coarse
description: Represent increasingly distant divisions using team/class priors and high uncertainty where direct evidence is sparse.

title: Lower-division recursion must terminate
description: Do not recursively expand into a full model of every lower-division program.

title: Cross-division translation is learned, never hard-coded
description: No fixed conference/division point penalty; estimate translation from historical cross-level evidence with uncertainty.

title: Use continuous strength rather than conference/division labels alone
description: Conference or division may inform priors but cannot replace continuous strength estimates.

title: Sparse/regime/lower-division evidence widens epistemic uncertainty
description: Explicitly carry uncertainty from sparse state, regime change, data quality and cross-division translation.

title: OOD/uncertainty does not force prediction direction
description: Out-of-distribution or sparse evidence generally widens uncertainty; it does not automatically favor either team.

title: Team-state representations require chronological comparison
description: Compare state alternatives through chronological/walk-forward evidence with early-season and transition subgroups before empirical selection.

title: W11 freezes interface but selects no empirical winner
description: Synthetic/reference tests may validate semantics but cannot declare a weighting/blend/translation representation predictively superior.

title: Roster membership is distinct from depth/availability
description: Official roster membership may not imply starter status, expected usage or availability.

title: Player roster/depth state is effective-dated
description: Roster, position, depth and role observations preserve PIT/effective intervals instead of overwriting historical state.

title: Depth observations preserve observed versus inferred status
description: Inferred depth/role evidence must retain confidence/provenance and may not be relabeled official.

title: Same-game participation cannot backfill pregame depth
description: Actual snaps/participation may evaluate prior expectations but cannot become same-game pregame ground truth.

title: Rotation and expected usage are first-class player state
description: Position-group state supports expected snap/opportunity distributions beyond a starter/backup binary.

title: Player value is position-aware and PIT-safe
source_basis: master W12; source chat; recon availability policy
description: Player value uses position/role-appropriate eligible evidence and explicit uncertainty.

title: No manual universal player or position point values
description: W12 freezes no rule assigning a fixed game-point value to a player or position.

title: Availability probability is distinct from effectiveness if active
description: Questionable/limited states represent both chance of participation and conditional effectiveness.

title: Expected usage is distinct from availability
description: Active status does not imply full snap/opportunity share; usage/limitations are modeled separately.

title: Availability covers non-injury absences
description: Availability supports illness, suspension, discipline, academic absence, targeting carryover, personal absence, opt-out and snap limits.

title: Availability evidence preserves source confidence and freshness
description: Every availability observation retains provenance, freshness, report/version and confidence class.

title: Missing availability evidence never implies healthy
description: Noncoverage or missing report produces UNKNOWN absent other eligible evidence.

title: Replacement identity/value/usage are explicit
description: Replacement impact identifies actual candidate replacement(s), their value, expected usage and uncertainty.

title: Replacement may redistribute across multiple players
description: Rotation or role changes may redistribute usage across multiple players rather than one backup.

title: Availability impact avoids duplicate injury encodings
description: Starter-out, injury count, team injury index and replacement gap may not all be stacked without incremental evidence.

title: Player availability hands off to W11 available strength
description: Player/availability/replacement state is the structured input for later derivation of available_strength from underlying_strength.

title: Prospects with zero college production use separate priors
description: Freshmen/prospects with no college snaps do not use transfer-production translation.

title: Prospect priors retain wide uncertainty
description: Recruiting/physical/development priors are uncertain until PIT-safe college evidence accumulates.

title: Transfer episodes preserve canonical player identity
description: Team/role transitions create episodes, not new player identities.

title: Transfer timing and destination knowledge are PIT-safe
description: Later destination/role information cannot enter forecasts before it was defensibly known.

title: Transfer translation uses continuous competition strength
description: Conference labels may inform context but cannot replace continuous source/destination strength evidence.

title: No fixed conference transfer penalty
description: Hand-authored rules such as G5-to-SEC minus X percent are prohibited.

title: Transfer translation uses historical same-player outcomes
description: Position-aware historical same-player transfers are the preferred training design where coverage supports it.

title: Transfer translation outputs value usage and uncertainty
description: Translation contracts expose expected destination value, role/usage, delta and uncertainty.

title: Preseason honors are timestamped consensus candidates
description: Honor observations preserve selector/scope/level/announced_at and receive no manual production bonus.

title: Postseason/future honors cannot leak into earlier games
description: Honor evidence is usable only after announcement and future postseason honors are banned for earlier forecasts.

title: Future NFL Draft outcomes are banned as same-season features
description: Eventual draft status/round/pick/combine outcomes cannot directly describe an earlier historical roster.

title: Lagged completed draft development is candidate evidence
description: Prior completed draft/program/position-development history may be tested with recruiting/talent controls.

title: Official conference availability lane is materialization priority
description: Covered official conference report archives are primary materialization targets; A&M/SEC receives highest-resolution priority.

title: Availability report materialization status is reported honestly
description: W12 source plans may not imply the historical availability archive is already downloaded/reconstructed.

title: Dataset source registry carries upstream rights/provenance
description: Dataset registry carries owner/access/auth/license/redistribution provenance sufficient for later acquisition/publication decisions.

title: Player-value decomposition predictive benefit is empirical hypothesis
description: Whether the W12 player-value/availability decomposition improves forecasts must be established by protected chronological evidence.

title: Transfer/honor/development candidate value is empirical hypothesis
description: Transfer translation, preseason honors and lagged draft-development value must earn promotion through protected testing.

title: Effective-dated coach role episodes
source_basis: Master prompt W13 + recon coach-role policy
description: Coach employment/responsibility must be represented as effective-dated role episodes with source/known-at evidence.

title: Coach title and responsibility separation
description: Formal title and actual unit/play-caller responsibility must remain separately representable.

title: Coach contribution from performance versus expectation
description: Coach-effect candidates should use performance residuals after controlling for talent/context rather than raw unit output.

title: Hierarchical partial pooling for sparse coach evidence
description: Low-sample coach-role effects should shrink toward role/family priors or an empirically superior alternative.

title: Coach promotion evidence without additive double counting

title: BAS labels are immutable/versioned

title: BAS inference clusters by canonical game

title: Aggie Excess is a null-first hypothesis
description: A&M-specific excess underperformance is a candidate effect; no-excess is an allowed conclusion.

title: BAS peer cohorts are predeclared/PIT-safe
description: Peer definitions must be frozen from PIT-safe/context evidence before protected outcomes are inspected.

title: BAS stability is tested across seasons/regimes
description: Any A&M excess/component claim must survive chronological season/regime stability checks.

title: Special Teams BAS requires anti-double-counting controls
description: Special-teams BAS must control overlap with hidden yards, field position and other duplicated value signals.
